cases.heading: All case styles
cases.title: Title Case
cases.hint: Multi-line input is converted line by line. Acronyms and numbers are split correctly (XMLHttpRequest2 → xml_http_request2).

list.title: Join into a list
list.hint: One item per line. Empty lines are skipped; if every item is a number, no quotes are added (leading zeros stay strings).

replace.title: Find & replace
replace.plainHint: Finds the exact text and replaces every occurrence.
replace.regexHint: In the replacement you can use $1·$2 (groups), $& (whole match), \n (newline), \t (tab). Regex steps are skipped when the input exceeds {max} characters.

affix.title: Add prefix / suffix to each line

pipeline.title: Clean up lines & whitespace — step by step
pipeline.hint: Add steps and move them up or down to update the result instantly. Undo or redo up to 30 additions, moves, removals and resets.
pipeline.empty: No steps yet. Tap a button to add one. The output currently shows your input unchanged.

errors.badRegex: Invalid regex — this step is skipped.
errors.tooLong: Input exceeds {max} characters, so the regex step is skipped.

textConverter.title: Text Converter
textConverter.description: Paste once to see 12 case styles side by side (UPPER, Title Case, camelCase, snake_case and more), then chain line tools: sort, dedupe, find & replace, and an SQL IN list builder.

howItWorks.title: How words are split
items: At separators such as space, _, -, . and /: user_id-name → user, id, name
At a lowercase-to-uppercase change: getUserName → get, User, Name
Runs of capitals (acronyms) stay together and split before the next capitalized word: XMLHttpRequest → XML, Http, Request
Digits stick to the preceding word: Request2Parser → request2, parser / HTML5Parser → html5, parser
Scripts without case (e.g. Korean) are kept as-is and split where they meet Latin letters: 주문Id → 주문, Id

whatIs.title: What is the Text Converter?
whatIs.description: Paste text once and see UPPER, lower, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, SCREAMING_SNAKE, kebab-case, Train-Case, dot.case and path/case all at the same time, then copy the one you need. The step tools below let you chain line sorting, de-duplication, empty-line removal, find & replace (regex), full/half-width conversion and SQL IN / JS array generation.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Paste your text into the input. Multi-line input is converted line by line.
In 'Every case at once', press the copy button next to the format you need.
Add steps, move them up or down, or remove them individually. Undo or redo up to 30 step changes and resets while preserving your source text and unfinished fields.

Copy the result with the button or Ctrl/Cmd + Enter. Shared links include only simple operations and list formats. Source text, find/replace text, prefixes, suffixes and history are excluded, and shuffle order may differ.

tips.title: Tips
items: IDs copied from a spreadsheet → Trim → Remove empty lines → Remove duplicates → SQL IN gives you a ready-made WHERE id IN (...) clause.
Paste several snake_case API field names and copy the camelCase versions in one go.
Sorting is natural, so file2 comes before file10.
Use 'Line breaks → space' for text copied from PDFs, and 'Full-width → half-width' for ＡＢＣ１２３ from CJK documents.
With regex on (m flag), replacing ^ with '- ' turns every line into a bullet.

items.q: What is the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?
items.a: camelCase starts lowercase and capitalizes later words (myVariable). PascalCase capitalizes every word (MyClass). Variables and functions usually use camelCase; classes and components use PascalCase.

items.q: Does it work with Korean text?
items.a: Korean has no letter case, so characters are kept and only word separators change (사용자 이름 → 사용자_이름). Sorting follows Korean order, and character reversal works on whole graphemes so Hangul and emoji never break. For initial-consonant extraction or romanization, use the Korean initials / jamo / romanization tool.

items.q: What rules does Title Case follow?
items.a: Every word is capitalized except articles, short prepositions and conjunctions (a, an, the, and, or, of, to, in, on, at…) that are neither the first nor the last word. Words that already mix cases, like NASA or iPhone, are preserved unless most of the line is in capitals.

items.q: How are names with acronyms and numbers split?
items.a: XMLHttpRequest2Parser is split into XML / Http / Request2 / Parser, so snake_case gives xml_http_request2_parser. Digits stay attached to the preceding word.

items.q: Is my text sent to a server?
items.a: No. Everything runs in your browser, and shared links contain only the names of the selected steps, never your text.

history.scope: Undo or redo up to {max} additions, moves, removals and resets. This affects transformation steps only, preserving your source text and unfinished find/replace fields. History lasts only while you stay on this page.
history.removed: Removed step {position}, {step}. You can undo this.
history.undone: Undid the step change. {remaining} undo actions remain.
history.redone: Redid the step change. {remaining} redo actions remain.
history.cleared: Cleared all {count} steps. Your source text is unchanged and you can undo this.
history.stepFailed: This step could not be applied and was skipped.
history.keyboard: With focus in the step list, use Alt+Up/Down to move a step. In this section, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes. Native undo in the source editor is unchanged.
history.urlNotice: Shared links restore only simple operations and list formats. Source text, find/replace text, prefixes, suffixes and history are excluded, and shuffle order may differ. Loading another shared setup starts a new history.
